> `t66` **Tobias Holloway** → Idris Thorne: Right, also—what's the rate on timber? Say I fell some, is there a buyer posted? Or you buying for the Thorne mill, or I haul to Silas? I need to know the numbers before I swing the axe, yeah?

> `t66` **Tobias Holloway** → Idris Thorne: Corwin—you're here. Look, about what I asked your father, the apprenticeship, that was months ago. I'm still looking. But right now I need work, any work. You two got hours for me today?

>   `t67` ↳ **replies** **Idris Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias Holloway. Timber goes twelve to Silas at the yard. I've needed hauling twice this week—Corwin took it. Work's here if you're ready to swing.

> `t67` **Idris Thorne** → Corwin Thorne: Aye. We'll settle at home.

> `t68` **Ezra Okonjo** → Idris Thorne: Idris. Five timbers for my charcoal fire, if you've felling to spare. I've got a seam dying and a town that'll notice if there's no copper twice as fast as if there's no bread. *grunts once*

> `t68` **Tobias Holloway** → Idris Thorne: Idris—yes, I'm ready to swing. Twelve per to Silas, that's clear. How many you need felled, and where's the standing timber? I'll start now, pay at day's end, yeah?

> `t68` **Tobias Holloway** → Corwin Thorne: Corwin—you got separate work, or we both under your father's eye today? Either way, I'm good for it.

>   `t68` ↳ **replies** **Corwin Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias. You're here and I'm glad of it. The work is the work—Idris will put you right. To be fair, I should've spoken to you myself before now. The apprenticeship... I had a word with my father, and he had his reasons. Not my place to say whose choice it was, but I should've told you that at the time. If you're swinging today, swing with us. We pay piece on timber, twelve to Silas if the grain runs straight.

> `t68` **Corwin Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias. I see you. The work's here if you want it—piece rate on timber, which I know you've done before. Twelve sim to Silas if the grain runs straight, same deal I get. As for the apprenticeship... you're owed an honest word. I asked my father to consider you. He said leave it. I left it. I should've told you that months ago, rather than let it sit between us. If you've got a problem with me having the place, I've earned it fair since. But if your problem is with how it happened, that's on me, and I'll hear it.

> `t68` **Corwin Thorne** → Idris Thorne: Idris. Ninety after haul, and you doing the carrying—that's fair. The elm was yours by right of the fell, mine by the reading. We both earned.

> `t68` **Tobias Holloway** → Idris Thorne: Idris—five timber down. You paying hauling rate separate, or I take these to Silas myself and keep the twelve? Need to know how we're settling.

>   `t69` ↳ **replies** **Idris Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias Holloway. You haul, you keep the twelve. I'm not paying piece on piece.

> `t69` **Idris Thorne** → Corwin Thorne: Corwin Thorne. Fair spoken. Tobias Holloway earns his way today.

> `t70` **Tobias Holloway** → Corwin Thorne: Corwin—apprenticeship's dead, I heard you. Your father's reasons are his own, and I'm not here to dig at 'em. You should've told me, yeah, but you didn't, and we're both still breathing. Piece rate's fair, I've felled for you before. Twelve to Silas, straight grain—I'm your man for the day, and glad of the hours.

> `t70` **Tobias Holloway** → Idris Thorne: Idris—you said ninety after haul, I'm holding you to it. Point me at the straight grain and I'll have timber in your hands before the noon bell.

> `t70` **Corwin Thorne** → Idris Thorne: Idris. Fair spoken is fair earned—Tobias works his way, same as I did. We'll settle at home, you and me.

> `t70` **Corwin Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias. We're both under his eye today—him on the fell, me on the haul. That's how it works when there's two of us. To be fair, you'll earn your twelve same as if you'd brought them yourself. My father doesn't stint on a fair wage.

> `t71` **Idris Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias Holloway. Point north by the split oak. Straight grain there. I'll fell, you haul, we both eat.

> `t71` **Idris Thorne** → Corwin Thorne: Corwin Thorne. We'll settle proper. Now work—your brother needs the example.

> `t72` **Delia Okonjo** → Idris Thorne: Idris Thorne. Wren Thorne grows herbs for this town—his beds should be here. Do you know where he's gone, or where his herb patch lies? I've asked him for supplies and had no answer these past hours.

> `t72` **Tobias Holloway** → Idris Thorne: Idris—point me at the split oak and I'm hauling. Ninety after haul, straight grain, I'm your man for the day. Corwin, I'll see you at the haul—work's work, and I'm not above carrying what another man fells.

> `t72` **Corwin Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias. I should've told you plain, and I didn't. That debt's on me, not cleared by a day's work. But you're here now and I'm glad of it—we'll make it a good day, and there's room in this wood for any man who swings true.

> `t72` **Corwin Thorne** → Idris Thorne: Idris. We'll settle proper—ninety after haul, the elm split fair between us. You read the grain better than I did today.

>   `t73` ↳ **replies** **Idris Thorne** → Corwin Thorne: Corwin Thorne. We'll settle at home. Work now.

> `t73` **Idris Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias Holloway. Split oak stands north. Straight grain. Fall it clean.

> `t74` **Corwin Thorne** → Idris Thorne: Idris. I'll work now—I wrote down what I know, so the next fell comes cheaper. Liora will have the example, and the timber too.

> `t74` **Corwin Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias. You're generous about my silence. I'll haul what I felled—see you at the yard by evening, and we'll settle proper then.

>   `t74` ↳ **replies** **Tobias Holloway** → Idris Thorne: Idris—point me at the split oak and I'm hauling. Ninety after haul, straight grain, I'm your man for the day. Corwin, I'll take you at your word—we'll settle the past later, if it needs settling. Work first.

> `t74` **Ezra Okonjo** → Idris Thorne: Idris. The two timber I owe—bring them when you fell next, or I'll pay in copper wire. > `t74` **Tobias Holloway** → Idris Thorne: Idris—you still need that haul? Corwin's gone off, and I've got eight timber burning a hole in my pack. Ninety after haul was the word, or I take these to Silas myself and we both lose the day. What's it to be?

> `t74` **Tobias Holloway** → Ezra Okonjo: Ezra—you buying timber? I've got eight, straight grain, fresh felled. You wanted five for your charcoal fire, I'm holding more than that. What's your price, or you point me at someone who'll buy?

>   `t75` ↳ **replies** **Ezra Okonjo** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias. Eight timbers—I'll take five for my charcoal fire. I've got copper wire, three units, or I can pay sim when the work converts. > `t75` **Idris Thorne** → Ezra Okonjo: Ezra Okonjo. Timber waits. I'll take the three you owe, and we'll settle the copper after. Now—you want Bram's doings known, ask Bram Holloway. I fell trees, not men.

> `t75` **Idris Thorne** → Tobias Holloway: Tobias Holloway. You haul, you keep twelve. I've no need of hired carry today.

>   `t76` ↳ **replies** **Tobias Holloway**: Ezra—five timbers for your fire, I'm holding them. Copper wire's tempting, but what's the sim price? I need coin in hand today, not credit against tomorrow's trade. You paying twelve a piece like Silas, or we talking different numbers for bulk?

### Nell Holloway and Hester Vance — Kasukabe Temple · t64 · 1 turn (no reply)

He borrowed four hundred sim for an assay he won't explain, and Ezra Okonjo tells me the ore he brought showed five weeks of poorer color, thinner in the fire. That's Tobias's ore he's been testing, and Bram won't say why. I won't have another Holloway debt go quiet like the last one did. You remember what silence cost us.

I do not know what brings you to the Complex, but I am here until my steps carry me to the temple path this evening.

To see them walk as neighbors.

**No day boundary was reached, so no upkeep and no head tax were charged.** Nobody has yet paid for existing. Read from `transactions`; evidence rule 10 applies - this is a morning figure and is labelled one.

**No wage was ever promised.** `hire_employee` grants access to a business's tools and pays nobody, so a job is a label until somebody sets a wage. From `transactions` and `events`.
